entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10495"/><div sID="gen18712" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10495"/><hi type="bold">17. dwelt--</hi>for a time, until they were ready for their journey to Egypt (<reference osisRef="Jer.42.1-Jer.42.22">Jr 42:1-22</reference>).<div eID="gen18712" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18713" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">habitation to Chimham--</hi>his "caravanserai" close by Beth-lehem. David, in reward for Barzillai's loyalty, took Chimham his son under his patronage, and made over to him his own patrimony in the land of Beth-lehem. It was thence called the habitation of Chimham (Geruth-Chimham), though it reverted to David's heirs in the year of jubilee. "Caravanserais" (a compound Persian word, meaning "the house of a company of travellers") differ from our inns, in that there is no host to supply food, but each traveller must carry with him his own. <div eID="gen18713" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10496"/><div sID="gen18714" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10496"/><hi type="bold">18. afraid--</hi>lest the Chaldeans should suspect all the Jews of being implicated in Ishmael's treason, as though the Jews sought to have a prince of the house of David (<reference osisRef="Jer.41.1">Jr 41:1</reference>). Their better way towards gaining God's favor would have been to have laid the blame on the real culprit, and to have cleared themselves. A tortuous policy is the parent of fear.
